paragraphs: The league got off to a tight start. **Wedd** led with 53, built on picks nobody else counted: Palmer's 13, Saka's 9 and Giles's 6, the last arriving as an auto-sub, with nothing wasted on his bench. **Mariswamy** was one point behind on 52, helped by a unique 9 from Calafiori, while **Ahuja** and **Klotz** finished level on 47, with Dewsbury-Hall's 11 the standout for Klotz and Mosquera's 6 Ahuja's best unique pick. Guéhi, owned by four managers, was the most widely shared big score with 10. The top four were separated by just six points, and **Mariswamy** also had Truffert auto-subbed in for Konsa.

**Croft** had the roughest opening, scoring 25, the week's lowest, and leaving 14 points on his bench, 9 of them from Trafford. **Shao** managed 36 after captaining Thiago, who returned nothing, so the armband was worth zero, whereas **Mariswamy**, **Ahuja** and **Klotz** all captained Haaland for just 2 points (4 doubled), the same return **Wedd** and **Croft** got from Isak. **Ahuja** also left 17 points on his bench, including 6 each from Verbruggen and Gomez, and the league average was 43.3. **Croft** also had Pedro Porro auto-subbed out for N.Williams, and just 28 points separated first from last.

**Klotz** surged to joint first with the week's best score, 96, riding Haaland's 26 (13 doubled) and B.Fernandes's 23 plus a unique 9 from Cunha. **Mariswamy** matched his 143 total with 91, helped by Haaland and a unique 11 from Calafiori, so the two share the lead. **Wedd** fell from 1st to 3rd on 80 despite a unique 16 from captain Isak. He was one of two managers without Haaland, who returned 13 (26 doubled) for the four who owned and captained him. Gibbs-White's 13 was shared by **Ahuja** and **Shao**, and the four Haaland owners all counted his 26.

**Croft** played his wildcard and scored 72, the week's lowest, leaving him last on 97, 14 behind **Shao** on 111. Shao's 75 came after captaining Thiago (2 points, 4 doubled) without Haaland in his side. **Klotz** left 13 points on the bench in Groß, and only three managers beat the league average of 83.2: **Klotz**, **Mariswamy** and **Ahuja**, whose 85 left him fourth on 132, 11 off the lead. **Wedd** had two auto-subs, Giles and Fatawu for Schuster and Watkins, **Shao** had Senesi replaced by Diop, and the gap from first to last grew to 46 points.

**Wedd** reclaimed first place on 199 with 66 points, led by a unique 26 from captain Isak (13 doubled) and 8 from the auto-subbed Giles. **Shao** actually posted the week's best score, 67, after playing his wildcard, with a unique 15 from Mitchell lifting him from 5th to 4th. **Mariswamy** and **Klotz**, who had shared the lead, dropped to second and third after scoring 51 and 45. **Mariswamy**, **Ahuja** and **Croft** each made one transfer this week, while **Wedd** and **Klotz** made none. Isak's 26 and Mitchell's 15 were the two biggest counted hauls that no one else shared.

Haaland returned 9 (18 doubled) for everyone who captained him, so **Wedd**'s armband on Isak was worth eight points more. **Croft** stayed last on 151 and left 19 points on his bench, 14 of them from Bogle, while **Mariswamy** left Damsgaard's 8 on the bench despite a unique 10 from Ødegaard. **Ahuja** had the week's lowest score, 42, and slipped to 5th on 174, with the whole table separated by 48 points. Haaland was in five of the six teams, **Wedd**'s being the exception.

**Croft** produced the week's best score, 94, by a distance, lifting him from 6th to 5th on unique returns from Bogle (15), De Cuyper (11) and Rogers (8). **Ahuja** moved up to 4th with 79, helped by unique hauls from Gabriel (9), Verbruggen (8), Gibbs-White (8) and Igor Jesus (7). **Shao** went the other way, dropping from 4th to last on 58 after making two transfers. **Croft**'s 94 was 15 clear of the next best, **Ahuja**'s 79, and about 24 above the league average of 69.7.

**Wedd** still leads on 259, four ahead of **Mariswamy**, with only 23 points between first and last. His captain Isak returned 2 (4 doubled) while Haaland gave the other five 18 once doubled, and Davis's 14 was a unique return. **Klotz** left 17 points on his bench, all of them Groß's again, and had two auto-subs, Diop and Konsa, replacing Hume and Shaw. **Shao** made two transfers without taking a hit and left nothing on his bench. **Mariswamy**, **Klotz** and **Ahuja** all sit within six points of **Wedd**.

Gameweek 5 turned a tight table upside down. **Shao** had the week of the league with 64 points, powered by 17 from Semenyo, a player no one else counted, plus 7 from Mitchell and a bench that wasted nothing, to jump from 6th to 3rd. **Croft**'s 58 lifted him from 5th to 2nd on the back of 10 apiece from Trafford and Willock, again picks unique to him. **Mariswamy** went the other way: second going into the week, he managed just 31, his lowest of the season, with little beyond Haaland's 12 and 4 apiece from Guéhi and Gvardiol to show for two transfers, and dropped to last.

**Wedd** stays top, but only just, and did it differently from everyone else: he was the only manager without Haaland, instead banking 16 from his captain Isak and 14 from Schuster, neither counted by anyone else. The other five all captained Haaland, who returned 12 once doubled, so Wedd's armband was worth four points more. **Croft** sits seven points behind and the whole table is separated by just 24. **Klotz** left 15 points on his bench, 14 of them from Groß, in a 42-point week, while **Ahuja** slipped to 5th on 42 despite three transfers. João Pedro not featuring forced auto-subs for four managers.

Gameweek 6 flipped the table on its head. **Ahuja** produced the week's best score, 72, to leap from 5th to 1st, with O'Shea's 11 (an auto-sub for the non-playing Szoboszlai) and Verbruggen's 9 both picks no one else counted. **Klotz** climbed from 4th to joint second on 67, led by unique returns from Dewsbury-Hall (13) and Cunha (10). The fallers were **Wedd**, who dropped from 1st to 4th with 39, his lowest of the season after captain Isak and Watkins both played 0 minutes, and **Shao**, who slid from 3rd to last after taking the league's first transfer hit of the season, 4 points for two moves, and scoring 47.

**Ahuja** now leads on 367, four ahead of **Klotz** and **Croft**, who are level on 363, and just 20 points separate first from last. João Pedro, missing a week earlier, returned 12 for all four managers who owned him, and Haaland's 6 became 12 for the four who captained him. **Shao** owned Haaland but captained Saka (2 points, 4 doubled), and the armband on Haaland instead would have been worth four more points. **Croft** left 22 points on his bench, 13 of them from Dewsbury-Hall, who returned 13 in **Klotz**'s XI, while **Mariswamy** moved up to 5th on 348, helped by a unique 9 from Calafiori.

**Ahuja** extended his lead with the week's best score, 65, built on Haaland's 26 (13 doubled) and unique returns from Gomez (8) and Verbruggen (6), after O'Shea came in as an auto-sub for Gibbs-White. **Mariswamy** was next on 58, helped by a unique 6 from Calafiori, and climbed from 5th to 4th, while **Shao** also rose a place to 5th on 54, with White's 6 his best unique pick. **Wedd** went the other way, falling from 4th to last on 34, the week's lowest and his lowest of the season, with Isak's 18 accounting for more than half of it.

**Ahuja** leads on 432, 15 clear of **Croft** on 417, with **Klotz** three further back on 414 and 49 points between first and last. All five managers who own Haaland captained him, and his 13 became 26, while **Wedd**, again the only manager without him, got 18 from captain Isak, eight fewer. **Klotz** left 14 points on his bench, including Konsa's 9, a player three other managers counted, and had Shaw replaced by Diop. Guéhi, owned by four managers, returned just 1, and **Ahuja**, **Croft** and **Mariswamy** each made two transfers without a hit.

**Mariswamy** had the week's best score, 59, helped by a unique 13 from N.Jackson and Roefs's 9, to climb from 4th to 3rd. **Klotz** rose from 3rd to 2nd on 52, and the auto-subs did the heavy lifting: Konsa, whose 9 points sat unused on his bench a week earlier, came in for B.Fernandes and returned 14, a score four managers counted. **Ahuja** stayed top but managed only 42, leaving 14 points on his bench, 9 of them from Roefs, while **Croft** dropped from 2nd to 4th on 46 with Trafford's 10 also stuck on the bench.

**Ahuja** leads on 474, eight clear of **Klotz**, with **Mariswamy** and **Croft** on 465 and 463, so the top four are within 11 points and 57 separate first from last. All six managers captained Haaland for the first time, and his 8 became 16 for each of them. João Pedro did not play, forcing auto-subs for **Ahuja**, **Klotz**, **Mariswamy** and **Croft**. **Shao** scored 45 with unique 10s from White and Tavernier, while **Wedd** made five transfers yet matched last week's 34, the week's lowest, and stayed last on 417.
